newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-SHOWCASE-MATCH ANALYSIS OF JUVENTUS V VICENZA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SHOWCASE-MATCH ANALYSIS OF JUVENTUS V VICENZA.

text.p: Following is an analysis of the strengths and weaknesses of Juventus and Vicenza who meet in Italy's serie A in Turin on Saturday (1500 GMT):

Playing style: Coach Marcello Lippi, having used 4-3-3 formation to win the European Cup and occasionally opting for a 4-3-2-1 line-up, falls back on 4-4-2 with many of his key players absent through injury or suspension. Michele Padovano and Christian Vieri will be the attack.

Strengths: Juventus boast the tightest defence in all of serie A, conceding just 15 goals in 21 matches. However, they are also the lowest scorers of the top six teams. The defence, unscathed by injury, looks solid with Ciro Ferrara and Paolo Montero twin pillars of strength and Angelo Di Livio vital in midfield. The club, with a high-achieving and vastly experienced squad, has probably the strongest team spirit in Italy. Not easily rattled and never underestimated.

Weaknesses: Lack of most of the household names in the squad. Zinedine Zidane (disqualified), Didier Deschamps, Angelo Peruzzi, Alen Boksic, Alessandro del Piero (all injured). The formation for Saturday may take time to click.

Motivation: Juventus need to pick up the pace after a 1-1 draw against Fiorentina at the weekend. But they will stay top even if they lose and the European Cup tie against Norway's Rosenborg next Wednesday is their main preoccupation.

Starting line-up (probable): Michelangelo Rampulla; Gianluca Pessotto, Ciro Ferrara, Paolo Montero, Mark Iuliano; Attilio Lombardo, Alessio Tacchinardi, Vladimir Jugovic, Angelo Di Livio; Michele Padovano, Christian Vieri.

Playing style: Often uncompromising, hard-tackling, occasionally long-ball and above all zonal at a time when the style championed by Arrigo Sacchi seems to be going out of fashion. There are no prima donnas, a lot of solid professionals who have seen hard times in the lower divisions and know their limitations. Their Italian Cup semifinal against Bologna on Tuesday was littered with tactical fouls.

Strengths: Good team spirit, with morale on a high after reaching cup final. Can count on a full strength line-up and have no shortage of stamina. Uruguayan Marcelo Otero, scorer of 12 goals this season, is prime danger man up front.

Weaknesses: Not really in the same class as Juventus, substituting drive and determination for raw talent, and while unaffected by injury they could be tired after playing an emotionally draining cup semifinal on Tuesday night. Saturday's game will be their third in five days.

Motivation: Every point brings them closer to a place in Europe, a feat they have achieved only once before. After reaching the cup final for the first time in 95 years, Vicenza may feel anything is possible. They have beaten Juventus on last two meetings, both 2-1 in Vicenza. Recent form has paled considerably since they led league before Christmas.

Starting line-up (probable): Luca Mondini; Luigi Sartor, Davide Belotti, Giovanni Lopez, Gilberto D'Ignazio; Domenico Di Carlo, Giampiero Maini, Fabio Viviani, Massimo Beghetto; Roberto Murgita, Marcelo Otero.

Referee: Massimo De Santis, 34. Employed by the Justice ministry in Rome. Has refereed 10 serie A matches, none with Juventus. Has a reputation for frequently interrupting play. His last serie A match was Reggiana v Milan in December, when he sent off Reggiana's Filippo Galli and awarded two penalties.
